{{Short description|Mathematical operation on matrices}}
{{No footnotes|date=November 2024}}
'''Min-plus matrix multiplication''', also known as '''distance product''', is an operation on [[matrix (mathematics)|matrices]].

Given two <math>n \times n</math> matrices <math>A = (a_{ij})</math> and <math>B = (b_{ij})</math>, their distance product <math>C = (c_{ij}) = A \star B</math> is defined as an <math>n \times n</math> matrix such that <math>c_{ij} = \min_{k=1}^n \{a_{ik} + b_{kj}\}</math>. This is standard matrix multiplication for the semi-ring of [[Tropical geometry|tropical numbers]] in the min convention.

This operation is closely related to the [[shortest path problem]].  If <math>W</math> is an <math>n \times n</math> matrix containing the edge weights of a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]], then <math>W^k</math> gives the distances between vertices using paths of length at most <math>k</math> edges, and <math>W^n</math> is the [[distance matrix]] of the graph.

== References ==
* [[Uri Zwick]]. 2002. [http://doi.acm.org/10.1145/567112.567114 All pairs shortest paths using bridging sets and rectangular matrix multiplication]. ''J. ACM'' 49, 3 (May 2002), 289–317.
* Liam Roditty and Asaf Shapira. 2008. [https://dx.doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-70575-8_51 All-Pairs Shortest Paths with a Sublinear Additive Error]. ICALP '08, Part I, LNCS 5125, pp.&nbsp;622–633, 2008.
